findings.title: Canonical symlink privacy check bypassed through Vite @id-wrapped @fs URLs
findings.trigger: An existing file or directory symlink in apps/web points to a private .local file. Request /@id//@fs/<absolute-allowed-alias>/canary.json?import or ?raw&import from the allowed Web Origin. The independent probe exclusively created both aliases to a synthetic mode0600 canary, then removed them.
findings.actual: Middleware realpath lookup includes the unprocessed /@id/ prefix, produces ENOENT and calls next. Vite later unwraps /@id/, treats the resulting URL as explicit /@fs/, and loads through the allowed lexical symlink path. Both file and directory symlink cases returned HTTP200 JavaScript containing the fake private marker, despite normal /@fs paths returning403.
findings.expected: Any request variant resolving to .local or another forbidden real target must be rejected before static/transform/raw handlers can read it; the documented canonical symlink guarantee must hold across Vite ID wrappers.
rootCauseEvidence: apps/web/dev-boundary.ts:57-73 candidate selection and ENOENT fallback
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize supported Vite request wrappers before realpath authorization, or enforce canonical file-target authorization in a resolver/load boundary covering every transformed ID. Preserve intended virtual modules and normal shared dependency loading. Extend regression coverage to @id-wrapped @fs requests through both directory and file symlinks with raw/import variants.
findings.testDefect: New regression only probes /@fs and normal paths; its file-symlink checks do not reach the @id-wrapped resolver path. All existing checks can pass while this bypass remains.
findings.reproducibilityEvidence: api-audit/runtime-probes.json: results/privateFakeMarkerLeaks entries labeled wrapped-fs-alias and wrapped-fs-method-variant; exclusively-owned fixture paths and cleanup are in ownership. Existing probe source/privacy-probe.py is preserved; no new probes performed during report completion.

completionMode: Documentation only; existing observations and read-only integrity verification
